decisions.reason: Particle-therapy QA is a narrower and more uncertain niche and this product showed weaker commercialization signals than the others, but it still fits the firm's core dosimetry capabilities so the option is worth keeping open for now.
A small-volume ionization chamber is close to the firm's established measurement business, and with no clear negative market signal the likely low carrying cost supports retaining it.

This chamber also sits squarely in the firm's core product family, and absent evidence of clear failure a specialist German med-tech firm would usually continue offering it while demand uncertainty resolves.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models is highly aligned with the firm's main customer base and installed workflow, making withdrawal within a year unlikely.
Relative dosimetry chambers are a natural complement to the firm's QA portfolio, so the firm would likely keep the product unless stronger evidence of weak uptake emerged.
A thimble ionization chamber is a core, established category for radiation measurement and likely inexpensive to support within the broader portfolio, so keeping it is the more probable choice.
